answer.decision: Use field-specific merge rules with monotonic account-status precedence and version metadata.
answer.action: Reconcile profile fields automatically using deterministic per-field version metadata and unique operation IDs. Resolve account status so suspended dominates active regardless of wall-clock ordering; permit reactivation only through an explicit reviewed-unsuspend operation. Retain operation metadata for idempotency, auditing, and reconciliation after partitions heal.
reasons: Wall-clock last-write-wins is unsafe because regional clock skew has reached 47 seconds.
Monotonic status precedence prevents stale active data from overriding a suspension while preserving the reviewed-unsuspend workflow.
Field-specific rules allow rare profile conflicts to converge automatically.
Keeping both regions writable satisfies the business-continuity requirement for partitions lasting up to one hour.
Existing unique operation IDs and identifiable reviewed-unsuspend operations provide key implementation primitives.
assumptions: Version metadata provides deterministic causal or logical ordering rather than relying solely on wall-clock timestamps.
All account-status transitions are covered by the defined precedence and reviewed-unsuspend rules.
A deterministic tie-breaker will be defined for concurrent profile updates that are otherwise unordered.
risks: Misclassifying a reviewed unsuspend could either prolong a suspension or cause improper reactivation.
Missing or inconsistently retained version metadata could produce divergent reconciliation results.
A deterministic profile-field tie-breaker may select a value users did not expect.
Implementation differences between regions could violate convergence or status-safety guarantees.

citations.claim: Regional clock skew has reached 47 seconds, making wall-clock last-write-wins unsafe.
Suspended must dominate active until an explicit reviewed unsuspend action occurs.
Both regions already attach unique operation IDs to writes.
Both regions must accept profile updates during partitions lasting up to one hour.
Conflict-resolution code can distinguish reviewed unsuspends from ordinary profile updates.
Profile conflicts occur in about 0.03 percent of multi-region edits.
